Added in 4.7.0, building on 4.6.0's Edge Relay edition. `internal/fleet` lets the
Gateway track registered edge relays, whether they're alive, and, for an
authorized operator, ask one to rebirth, restart, or adopt a newly pushed
config. Off by default (`HOTLOOP_FLEET_ENABLED`): a deployment with no edge
relays has no broker to point this at.

## What it is not

**Not the same thing as the MQTT driver's Sparkplug host mode.**
`internal/driver/mqtt.go` polls tag values out of whatever Sparkplug nodes a
configured Device connects it to, one Device row is one broker connection,
built for tag consumption. Fleet management owns its own, separate MQTT
connection and answers a different question: is a *registered* edge relay
alive, not what value is on one of its tags. Bolting this onto the
tag-polling driver would have meant either forcing an operator to configure
a compatible Device just to get fleet visibility, or reaching into that
package's private per-node bookkeeping, which was never built to be shared.

**Not automatic.** An edge relay showing up on the broker does not make it a
fleet member. Membership is declared, a row in `fleet_members`, created
through `POST /api/fleet`, the same distinction this app already draws
between a tag a driver discovers and a tag someone configures. An NBIRTH
from a group/node nobody registered is logged at debug and otherwise
ignored.

## How it fits together

Two data paths, both from `internal/fleet.Manager`'s own MQTT connection:

- **Presence**, from NBIRTH/NDEATH. Outbound-only from the relay's side, it
  dials the broker, same as it always does to publish readings, so this
  works through NAT with no inbound connection to the relay required.
- **Detail**, from an optional HTTP poll of the relay's own `/status` (see
  `docs/EDGE-RELAY.md`), only for members with a `statusUrl` registered.
  Fanned out concurrently with a short per-member timeout, the same shape
  `internal/api/sites.go` already uses for polling remote sites, an
  unreachable relay is marked `reachable: false`, never reported as a
  healthy zero.

Commands travel the other way over Sparkplug NCMD, extending what a relay
already handles:

- **Rebirth** (`Node Control/Rebirth`), already handled by every edge
  relay's `internal/edgepublish.Publisher` since 4.5.0. A benign,
  idempotent nudge.
- **Restart** (`Node Control/Reboot`, the Sparkplug spec's own name for this,
  not one this app invented), the relay publishes its own graceful NDEATH
  and exits; its supervisor (a Quadlet unit's `Restart=always`, or a
  Deployment's default `restartPolicy: Always`) brings it back up with
  whatever is on disk at that moment. No new shutdown path, this is the
  exact same clean-exit route the relay's own `SIGTERM` handling already
  takes.

Because commands ride the same MQTT connection the relay already dials out
on, sending one needs no inbound connection to the relay either.

A relay that shows up online can be commanded, full stop. Every relay
subscribes to its NCMD topic, and waits for the broker to confirm it, before
it publishes a birth, on every connection, so "Online" is never ahead of
"reachable." The manager holds itself to the same rule on its side: it does
not report itself started until its NBIRTH/NDEATH subscriptions are
confirmed, so a relay that births the instant the Gateway comes up is not
missed. If the broker's ACL refuses either side's subscription, that side
refuses to start and says so, instead of running half-deaf.

## Config push

Pushing what a relay polls doesn't ride NCMD, a Sparkplug metric isn't
sized for a whole device file, it goes to a **retained, plain MQTT topic**
per relay: `hotloop/edge-relay-config/<group>/<node>`. Retained
delivery is what makes this work with no separate "catch me up" request:
whatever was last published there is handed to any client that subscribes,
immediately, including a relay reconnecting after being offline, or
starting up for the very first time.

`POST /api/fleet/{id}/config` (`fleet.config`, admin-only, the same
narrowing as `fleet.restart`) parses and validates the device file **before
publishing anything**, using the identical rules `internal/edgerelay`
applies on the relay's own side, so a malformed push is a rejected API call,
not a relay quietly stuck with something broken. The relay validates again
on receipt, this app cannot assume nothing except the Gateway can ever
publish to that topic, only that it should refuse to publish something
broken itself.

**A device file can carry credentials, and a push publishes it.** A device's
`config` block holds whatever its driver logs in with, such as an OPC UA
`username` and `password` (4.15.0), and the file is published as it is,
retained. Anyone who can subscribe to `hotloop/edge-relay-config/#` can read it,
so the broker needs TLS and an ACL on that topic before a file with credentials
is pushed. The Gateway's API hides device credentials from every role as of 4.15.1,
but a pushed file is not behind the API and is not changed by that. See
[EDGE-RELAY.md](/edge-relay/reference/#credentials-in-the-device-file-4150) and
[AUTH.md](/iot/authentication/#where-credentials-are-still-in-the-clear).

**A push applies live, and it never restarts anything.** Up to 4.17 a push
only staged the file, and making it count took a second action, a
`POST /api/fleet/{id}/restart`, which dropped the relay's broker session and
every device session it held to change one tag. Now:

- **A relay that's running** validates the file, saves it, and applies it in
  place: new devices connect, removed ones disconnect, changed ones
  reconnect, and every device that didn't change keeps its session. The
  Sparkplug session and the forward queue stay up the whole time. The node
  rebirths for its new metric set and nulls the metrics it dropped first, so
  a host doesn't keep showing a removed device's last good value.
  [EDGE-RELAY.md](/edge-relay/reference/#what-a-live-apply-keeps-and-what-it-changes)
  has exactly what goes out on the wire and why.
- **A file the relay refuses** (it won't parse, it won't validate, it can't
  be saved) changes nothing on the relay, and the relay's `/status` says so
  under `config.rejected`. `GET /api/fleet` shows that for every member with
  a `statusUrl`, next to the digest of the file it's running, so "I pushed it"
  and "it's running it" are two things you can check, not one you assume.
  The Gateway validates before it publishes too, so in practice this is a
  relay on a newer or older release disagreeing about the rules, or
  something other than the Gateway publishing to the topic.
- **A relay that's offline** gets the retained push the moment it connects.
  At boot it waits a couple of seconds for it before loading its local file
  (see `cmd/edge-relay/main.go`'s `applyPushedConfig`), so it comes up on the
  pushed list instead of starting on the old one and switching.

A pushed file lands on the relay's data volume, not over its local device
file, and wins over the local one until the push is cleared. The relay's
[EDGE-RELAY.md](/edge-relay/reference/#where-a-pushed-file-lives-and-which-file-wins)
has the precedence rules and the 4.16.0 bug that made them necessary.

**Taking a push back** is `DELETE /api/fleet/{id}/config` (`fleet.config`,
same as pushing). It publishes an empty retained message to the member's
config topic, which is how MQTT deletes a retained value, so no later boot
applies the push. A relay connected at the time drops its pushed file and goes
back to its local one live, the same way a push applies, unless its local file
doesn't load, in which case it keeps the pushed one and says so. A relay that
was offline never hears the clear (an empty message isn't retained), so send
it again once the relay is back.

## What each relay runs, and updates

Every relay puts its version and the digest of its image in each birth, and so
does an Edge or a Gateway with edge publish on, so a box registered here as a
member shows the same (string
metrics named `Node Info/Version` and `Node Info/ImageDigest`, with no alias, so
a Sparkplug host that doesn't know them ignores them). `GET /api/fleet` shows
them as `release` on each member: `version`, `imageDigest` and `since`, when the
Gateway first heard that build. A relay from before this reports none, and the
Gateway says nothing about it rather than invent an "unknown build".

When a member's build changes, the Gateway writes it to the system log as a
`config` event on that member, with the old and new version and digest in its
detail (`{"kind":"fleet.release",...}`). The first build it ever hears is
logged too, as the baseline the next one is measured against. It survives a
Gateway restart, because the last record is read back from the log: a restart
never invents an update. This is the audit trail of every update a relay takes,
by whatever route (Podman's timer, an approval, `helm upgrade`, somebody on the
box), because the Gateway doesn't cause an update and can only report it. A
moving tag is how `:stable` updates, so a changed digest under the same version
is logged too, as "a different image of the same version".

`POST /api/fleet/{id}/update` (`fleet.update`, admin-only) approves the update a
relay holds for. It only does anything to a relay set to hold updates; any
other relay logs that it ignored it. The request names no image. What this does
and doesn't do for each install type is in
[EDGE-RELAY.md](/edge-relay/reference/#updating-a-relay).

## Command authorization

Two layers, deliberately not one:

- **At the API**, an operator needs `fleet.rebirth` to request a rebirth;
  restarting, approving an update or pushing a config each need
  `fleet.restart`/`fleet.update`/`fleet.config`, granted only to admin. A restart is more disruptive to a running poll
  cycle than a rebirth nudge, and pushing what a relay polls is treated the
  same way, the same narrowing `alarms.ack` and `automations.trigger`
  already model for other "do it now" actions.
- **At the broker**, this app has no way to enforce anything, NCMD
  publishing and the config topic must both be restricted by the broker's
  own ACLs to the Gateway's own MQTT credentials. Without that, anything
  that can reach the broker and knows a relay's group/node can publish the
  same command or config this feature does. Configure this at deployment
  time; it is not optional just because it lives outside this app's own
  code.

## API

| Route | Permission | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/fleet` | `fleet.read` | Every registered member, with live presence and, where configured, a polled `/status` |
| `POST /api/fleet` | `fleet.write` | Create or update a member (a body with an existing `id` updates it) |
| `DELETE /api/fleet/{id}` | `fleet.write` | Remove a registered member |
| `POST /api/fleet/{id}/rebirth` | `fleet.rebirth` | Publish `Node Control/Rebirth` |
| `POST /api/fleet/{id}/restart` | `fleet.restart` | Publish `Node Control/Reboot` |
| `POST /api/fleet/{id}/update` | `fleet.update` | Approve the image update a relay is holding for (does nothing to a relay that isn't) |
| `POST /api/fleet/{id}/config` | `fleet.config` | Push a new device file (raw JSON body, validated before publishing); a running relay applies it live |
| `DELETE /api/fleet/{id}/config` | `fleet.config` | Clear the push, so the relay goes back to its local device file, live if it's connected |

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | <span class="sr-only">Details</span> |
|---|---|---|
| `HOTLOOP_FLEET_ENABLED` | `false` | The feature is off until this is set |
| `HOTLOOP_FLEET_BROKER` | n/a | Required when enabled. Bare host, `host:port`, or a full URL |
| `HOTLOOP_FLEET_USER` / `_PASSWORD` | n/a | Broker credentials |
| `HOTLOOP_FLEET_TLS` | `false` | |
| `HOTLOOP_FLEET_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY` | `false` | Per-deployment opt-in; never set this by default |

## What has and has not been verified

Tested against a real Mosquitto broker and a real
`internal/edgepublish.Publisher` standing in for an edge relay, not a
hand-rolled stand-in, the actual code every edge relay runs: presence
tracking on a real NBIRTH/NDEATH, a real rebirth round trip (the sent NCMD
observed by the relay's own already-tested command handler, and the
resulting second birth observed back by this package's own listener), a
real restart round trip against the `RestartRequested` channel, and
`/status` polling against both a real `httptest` server and a deliberately
unreachable address. Config push is tested the same way for the push itself
(a real retained publish, received by a real `Publisher.ConfigReceived`),
**and separately end to end through the actual compiled `cmd/edge-relay`
binary**, run as a real subprocess against a real broker: a config retained
*before the process even starts* is what it boots with, proving
`applyPushedConfig`'s boot-ordering claim rather than just its two pieces in
isolation.

**Not yet run against a certified Sparkplug host application** publishing
NCMD to this app, nor against a real broker's ACL configuration restricting
who may publish it, the authorization boundary described above is a
deployment requirement this app cannot verify from the inside, only
document.
